title: Krefeld 2025 lot 27: Hydractinia echinata / Blaschka no. 156 crosswalk
purpose: Resolve the catalogue-facing taxonomic identity of Krefeld lot 27, convert it into exact historical search keys, and cross-check those keys against the project's complete transcription of the published MfN OS001-02 inventory without overclaiming object identity or disposal history.

auction_record.title_raw_en: Glass model of a stinging polyp, around 1870
auction_record.label_transcription: Zoolog. Institut Universität, Berlin / handwritten botanical designation

taxonomic_resolution.identity_guard: Resolving the German object name to Hydractinia echinata does not identify this physical auction object with any surviving institutional specimen.

evidence.finding: The collection explicitly captions a Blaschka glass model as 'Stachelpolyp (Hydractinia echinata)'.

source.collection: Cornell Collection of Blaschka Invertebrate Models

blaschka_catalogue_resolution.guard: Blaschka no. 156 is a catalogue/model-design number and is not a unique serial number for one physical object. Multiple institutions could have ordered the same design.

mfn_os001_02_crosscheck.published_inventory: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, OS001-02 Blaschka Glasmodelle
mfn_os001_02_crosscheck.result: No Hydractinia echinata / Stachelpolyp entry and no Blaschka catalogue number 156 occurs in the complete 40-row OS001-02 transcription captured by the project backend.
mfn_os001_02_crosscheck.negative_scope: This is a strong negative for the presently published OS001-02 inventory only. It does not prove that Berlin never held a Hydractinia no. 156, that HU never held one, or that the auction object never passed through MfN before the current inventory was constituted.
mfn_os001_02_crosscheck.provenance_effect: A direct match between Krefeld lot 27 and a currently published MfN OS001-02 record is therefore unsupported. HU historical teaching-stock and reduction/dispersal records become the higher-priority route.

hu_branch.current_public_index_result: No Hydractinia echinata result was recovered in the current indexed public-portal pass.
hu_branch.public_index_guard: The HU public portal is not treated as a complete historical inventory, so this negative is weaker than the complete 40-row MfN cross-check.

documented_dispersal_window.event: HU records a decision to reduce the collection; some material was given away, many preparations were lost, and other parts were transferred to the Museum für Naturkunde.

rakow_design_archive_seed.finding: The Rakow Research Library MS 0013 finding aid includes a marine-invertebrate drawing entry for Hydractinia echinata within the Blaschka drawing series.
rakow_design_archive_seed.source: Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka Collection, MS 0013, Rakow Research Library finding aid
rakow_design_archive_seed.use: Potential future image/design comparison source after the auction-object imagery and exact drawing record are inspected at object level.
rakow_design_archive_seed.guard: Presence of a Hydractinia drawing does not establish provenance for the Krefeld object.

lot_26_control.reason: The auction record gives only 'sea anemone' plus a handwritten botanical designation not yet transcribed to a taxon. The complete MfN inventory contains several potentially relevant actiniarian/zoantharian records, but dimensions and broad morphology are insufficient for identification.
lot_26_control.guard: These are comparison candidates, not proposed identities.

provenance_hypothesis_update.strongest_current_hypothesis: Lot 27 was once part of HU/Zoologisches Institut teaching stock or another Berlin university zoological teaching sequence and later left that custody.
provenance_hypothesis_update.why_strengthened: The institutional label style is independently corroborated at HU; the taxon is now resolved to Hydractinia echinata and catalogue no. 156; that design is absent from the complete present MfN OS001-02 transcription; HU documents a later collection-reduction/dispersal event.
do_not_claim: that lot 27 definitely belonged to HU
that lot 27 was transferred to MfN
that the Krefeld circa-1870 date is wrong
that catalogue no. 156 uniquely identifies one physical specimen

next_actions: Search HU historical inventories and acquisition records for Hydractinia echinata, Stachelpolyp and Blaschka no. 156.
Search HU 1968-1970 reduction, gift, loss and transfer files for Hydractinia, no. 156 and old Zoologisches Institut inventory numbers.
Inspect Krefeld lot 27 photographs for any second label, handwritten species wording, catalogue number or old inventory number.
Inspect the Rakow MS 0013 Hydractinia echinata drawing record and image as a model-design comparison, without treating design similarity as provenance proof.
Keep Krefeld lot 26 taxonomically open until its handwritten designation or a stronger image/identifier bridge is recovered.
